name: Russian Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1914 Russian Empire polygons (21.31M + 0.18M km2) plus Finland (0.33M) = ~21.8M km2 computed on the sphere; B&H Table 1: 21.7M km2 exc. Finland plus 0.4M Finland.

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 1: Russian Empire exc. Finland 173.2M plus Finland 3.2M = 176.4M (1913, League of Nations 1927) (high); COW NMC v7 tpop 1914 = 175,100k (mid); B&H Table 9 (Urlanis) 167.0M (low).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Russia 1910 = 18.1% (present-day Russia, more urban than the empire). 1897 census 13.4% urban; ~15% by 1914 (mid). Low = COW upop/tpop 1914 = 10,479/175,100 = 0.06 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Cited page: peacetime strength ~1.3M in 1913 (811,000 infantry, 133,000 cavalry, 209,000 artillery, 59,000 engineers, 88,000 support); wartime mobilisation in 1914 increased this to 4.5M. High is a judgement bound below the cited page's 5,962,396 active and reserve troops. Navy (~55,000) included. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 1,321k, 1915 = 5,500k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Cited page: total active and reserve troops estimated at 5,962,396 in 1913, incl. first and second line reservists; after 4.5M were called the residual trained pool (older reserve classes, opolchenie 1st class with prior service) was ~1.5-3M. Reconstruction, grade C.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery (209,000 in peace on the cited page), engineers, support and auxiliary troops, depots, navy, staffs, scaled to the mobilised army.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total mobilised: 15,378,000 (Krivosheev) or 12,000,000 (US War Dept) on the cited page; divided by ~175M = 0.07-0.09. Low because of exemptions, illiteracy and the peasant economy, not lack of men.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Stone, The Eastern Front 1914-1917 (isbn:0-14-026725-5), not read from a fetched source. ~114 infantry divisions after mobilisation (70 first-line, 35 reserve) at ~16 battalions and ~16,000 rifles each, plus fortress infantry (Stone, The Eastern Front ch. 2). Peacetime infantry 811,000 (cited army page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: Mosin-Nagant rifle and Maxim MG adequate; rifle and shell shortages from autumn 1914

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training). Evidence: four-year conscription but low literacy; reservists poorly trained

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Stone, The Eastern Front 1914-1917 (isbn:0-14-026725-5), not read from a fetched source. Rifle brigades (Finnish, Siberian, Caucasian, Turkestan, ~16-20 brigades of 8 battalions).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: same weapons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Siberian rifle units rated the best Russian infantry

count.note: Educated guess. Peace strength read from the Imperial Russian Army page; wartime count recalled from Stone, not read from a fetched source. Cited page: 133,000 cavalrymen in peace; ~36 cavalry divisions after mobilisation incl. Cossack second- and third-line regiments (Stone ch. 2).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: lance, sabre and carbine; large but used poorly for reconnaissance

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Cossack hosts and regular cavalry, horsemanship strong

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Stone, The Eastern Front 1914-1917 (isbn:0-14-026725-5), not read from a fetched source. ~6,300 76.2 mm M1902 field guns, ~500 122 mm howitzers and ~240 heavy pieces with the field army (Stone ch. 2); peace establishment 3,904 guns (cited army page). Fortress guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 76 mm M1902 as good as the French 75; almost no modern heavy artillery; shell crisis from late 1914

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: poor infantry-artillery co-ordination

count.note: Cited page: Russia had the largest Entente air fleet at the outbreak, 263 aeroplanes; ~244 with the army in the field. Reconnaissance types; Ilya Muromets bomber squadron formed December 1914.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mostly French designs, engine shortages

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: few trained pilots and mechanics

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Conway's 1906-1921: ~9 pre-dreadnoughts (4 Baltic, 5 Black Sea) and ~14 armoured and protected cruisers (Rurik, Bayan class, Bogatyr class, Aurora, Pamiat Merkuria...) = 20/24/28, the 4 Gangut-class dreadnoughts commissioned in late 1914 (high); plus ~100 destroyers (Baltic, Black Sea and Pacific), incl. the modern Novik = 85/100/115. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.45/0.5/0.55 (24) and destroyers 0.5/0.55/0.6 (100), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.5 and 0.5-0.75. Evidence: pre-dreadnought fleet rebuilt after Tsushima; dreadnoughts not yet ready; Novik the fastest destroyer of 1914, many older boats

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers (24) and destroyers (100), both 0.5/0.55/0.6, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: training 0.5-0.75 and 0.5. Evidence: Baltic Fleet excellent at mine warfare (cited navy page); mine-laying and coastal operations

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. ~28 submarines, mostly small Holland and Lake types (Conway's).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: old small boats; Bars class completing 1915-16

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: limited sea time

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Samsonov and Rennenkampf failed to co-ordinate (Tannenberg, Masurian Lakes); Ivanov and Brusilov beat the Austrians in Galicia; faction-ridden high command

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5 (national conscript army). Evidence: peasant conscripts, many non-Russian; mass surrenders at Tannenberg (~92,000 prisoners)

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: patriotic rally of August 1914 (cited economic-history page); faded by 1915

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: Mosin-Nagant, Maxim MG, 76 mm M1902 QF; few heavy guns, chronic shell shortage

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: no helmets or armoured vehicles in 1914; Austin armoured cars from 1915

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts). Evidence: Gangut dreadnoughts completing late 1914, Novik destroyer; mostly pre-dreadnoughts

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts). Evidence: Novogeorgievsk, Kovno, Brest-Litovsk, Przemysl-type fortresses (Kovno and Novogeorgievsk fell in 1915)

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 (magazines) and 7 (railways). Evidence: rail network ~1/10 the density of Germany's; armies outran railheads in East Prussia

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: uncoded wireless orders intercepted before Tannenberg; telephone wire shortages

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance. Evidence: 263 aircraft but poor use of reconnaissance and cavalry

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914. Evidence: Sikorsky Ilya Muromets four-engine bomber, unique in 1914

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): USSR-territory 1913 = 2,254 (2011 int$), the series that matches B&H Table 1 (1,488 in 1990 int$ for the Russian Empire). The separate 'Russia' series in the same file gives 1,163 for 1913, inconsistent with the USSR aggregate and not used. Finland (1,140 in 1990 int$, B&H) pulls the average down slightly.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Ferguson, The Pity of War (isbn:0-7139-9246-8), not read from a fetched source. Low: defence ~4.5-5% of NNP in 1913 (Ferguson, Pity of War table 6, the highest burden of the powers relative to income). Mid/high: wartime share rising towards ~30% of national income by 1916; reconstruction, grade C.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry and mining ~20-25% of national income in 1913; agriculture ~half.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Cited page: the peasantry was 80% of the population at the turn of the 20th century; Collectivization in the Soviet Union page: 82% peasants in 1928. Population share used as a proxy for the agricultural employment share: 1 - 0.80 = 0.20 (mid). Russia was Europe's largest grain exporter in 1913.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. 1911 intake read from the Imperial Russian Army page; class size recalled from Stone, not read from a fetched source. Cited page: ~455,000 called up in 1911 out of a much larger liable class; the yearly class of men reaching 21 was ~1.3M (Stone ch. 2).

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1916; Russian output of 76 mm guns rose from ~40 per month in 1914 to several hundred per month by 1916.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Fighters per year 1915-1916 (domestic Nieuport, Morane and Sikorsky types); total Russian aircraft output ~1,500-1,900 per year by 1916.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Reconnaissance and bomber aircraft per year 1915-1916.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Dreadnoughts, cruisers and destroyers completed per year: dreadnoughts and cruisers 1914-1917 (4 Gangut 1914-15, 3 Imperatritsa Mariya 1915-17) = 0/2/4; Novik-type destroyers = 5/12/20. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Bars-class and AG-class submarines per year 1915-1917.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Metalled chaussees of the Russian Empire; most roads were unpaved tracks impassable in the rasputitsa.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Russia 1913 = 58,500 km plus Finland 1913 = 3,560 km = 62,060 km (mid). CHAT coverage of the Asiatic lines is not stated (Russia 1920 = 71,600 km in the same series), hence grade C.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. St Petersburg/Kronstadt, Reval, Riga, Libau, Helsingfors, Odessa, Sevastopol, Nikolaev, Archangel, Vladivostok.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914: Russian flag 974,178 GRT (steam and sail, 100 tons and over, Register Book 1913-14). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Russian armies in East Prussia outran their supply within ~100-150 km of the frontier railheads (break of gauge at the border).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses of the Russian Empire (~30-35M, the largest stock in the world); ~0.8-1.0M requisitioned in 1914.

basesAbroad.name: Port Arthur lease lost 1905; Harbin (CER zone)

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: familiar terrain, fortresses, deep strategic depth and a continental winter that invaders were not adapted to.

notes: Snapshot date August 1914 after mobilisation (general mobilisation 30-31 July). Territory and population = the Russian Empire in Europe and Asia including the Grand Duchy of Finland and Congress Poland (neither a separate state in 1914, so includes is empty; the finland and poland nationIds are later states). Bukhara and Khiva protectorates excluded. Forces are the whole army; on the German front in August the 1st and 2nd Armies had ~30 divisions, the four armies against Austria-Hungary ~53. Aircraft in aircraft_strike (no fighters in 1914). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Stone, Conway's, Ferguson) not fetched online, graded at most B.
